key_insight: LeanPRM uses Lean to automatically generate step-level correctness labels for natural-language proofs, avoiding costly human annotation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable training pipeline for proof verifiers that can improve step checking and proof selection across model sizes.
method: Generate a natural-language proof and a paired formal Lean proof with no Lean feedback.
Use Lean to label each proof step, then filter out syntax-only failures so negatives reflect mathematical errors.
Train a process verifier on the resulting step-labeled dataset.
evidence_signal: LeanPRM includes 10,634 proofs and 152K labeled steps; a Qwen3-4B verifier improved exact step-label accuracy on LeanPRM-Bench from 48.2 to 74.7, outperforming a PRM800K-trained baseline.
watch_item: Quality depends on the alignment between natural-language and formal Lean proofs, so formalization mismatches or noisy translations could still bias labels.
paper_title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
